description: #177 follow-up (บอง's review lens, caught before any PR-B run): in stack.sh up(), the LOCAL git-exclude for *.testenv-shadowed was written by ensure_local_ignore AFTER shadow_others had already renamed each prod .env* to that suffix — so between the rename and the exclude-write there was a window where a prod-secret file (mootech-be/.env.local carries SUPABASE_REAL_PRODUCTION_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_REAL_DB_PASSWORD, RENDER_API_KEY — RLS-bypassing + infra-controlling, the strongest creds we hold) sat on disk under a git-COMMITABLE name (git check-ignore .env.local.testenv-shadowed → not-ignored, verified in all 3 repos). Normally a blink, but if stack.sh dies mid-run (post-copy guard fail → exit) AND the rollback trap fails to un-shadow, the key is left exposed to a commit. Low probability, unrecoverable if it fires. Fix: order ensure_local_ignore BEFORE shadow_others (and before write_breadcrumb) so the shadowed file is born already-ignored — window = ZERO. Design was already correct (the *SHADOW_SUFFIX pattern goes into .git/info/exclude); only the call order was swapped. Teeth (shadow-ignore-order.test.sh, run under bash 3.2, neg-control-first): Part A behavioral — shadow-first leaves .env.local.testenv-shadowed NOT git-ignored (window reproduced), ignore-first makes it ignored the instant it exists; Part B structural — asserts stack.sh calls ensure_local_ignore before shadow_others, MUTANT reorder-back → RED CAUGHT. 5/5 fixed, mutant caught. Script-only, no runtime/TS touched. gate_layer=infra/shell (secret-at-rest exposure window).
